title: Consumer projection boundaries and operation-specific peer evidence
mode: Primary-source documentation review and local plan reconciliation
head: de27a3391a624aba03ca71f3583c4b3a6e6396a9
scope: Reconcile FreeCAD's documented importer profiles against the existing native consumer gate.
Separate GDAL Binary-DXF transport from OGR projection and writer-version evidence.
Use LibreDWG class-status and fuzz-target documentation to refine peer-result and scheduled hardening evidence.
Keep external work at composed checkpoints and preserve the plan's fast per-slice validation and fixture policy.

sources.name: FreeCAD Draft DXF and DWG route documentation
sources.observed: The documentation page distinguishes C++ and legacy DXF importer profiles, both starting at R12. The C++ profile lists 2D geometry, text, dimensions, leaders, layers and paper space, but skips text/dimensions/attributes inside blocks; the legacy profile differs and includes 3DFACE. Stock FreeCAD cannot read ACIS/SAT solids and DWG uses an external converter followed by the selected DXF importer. The documentation repository page is archived/read-only, and its broad no-loss sentence conflicts with its own explicit limitations.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Documentation defines candidate route profiles and scope only. The exact FreeCAD build, source revision, preferences, converter and runtime result must decide behavior; no application was run.

sources.name: GDAL DXF driver documentation
sources.observed: Binary-DXF reading starts in GDAL 3.12. The driver documents a direct Binary-DXF-to-ASCII translation path distinct from OGR projection. OGR projections may tessellate curves, simplify text, omit MLINE styling and HATCH fill, inline/merge blocks, and skip modeler entities by default; AC1027+ 3D-extensible mode exposes raw ASM bytes and a transform rather than geometry. Raw unhandled group values are opt-in, and the documented writer targets AutoCAD 2004.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Driver documentation establishes available routes and known projection limits, not exact runtime behavior for a local build or a general DXF round trip. No GDAL executable or drawing was run.

sources.name: LibreDWG manual and fuzz setup
sources.observed: The manual separates stable, unstable, debugging and unhandled classes, notes that unknown types may remain binary blobs without DXF codes, and says R2007 DWG writing is unavailable while pre-R13 DXF is in progress. The fuzz setup separates input, rewrite and output targets and triages crashes, hangs and leaks for regression replay.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Project documentation and workflow description only. It does not establish libdxfrw defects or runtime parity, and no peer campaign was run.

localEvidence: The existing PAR-07/S8 route ledger already separates source identity, carrier/owner closure, output, semantic evidence, and consumer acceptance; the new evidence sharpens denominator and projection-route rules rather than adding a parallel gate.
The existing validation policy uses focused local controls per slice and defers cross-platform FreeCAD, peer comparisons, and long fuzz to composed/scheduled checkpoints.
The FreeCAD documentation's generic 1:1/no-loss statement must not override the same source's explicit importer/converter limitations or observed runtime behavior.

assessment.planImpact: Refines only existing PAR-07/S8 and 7S owners. FreeCAD evidence is backend/profile-specific; GDAL direct Binary-DXF translation is separate from lossy OGR projection and its AutoCAD-2004 writer is not a modern target-version oracle; LibreDWG results are class-status and operation-specific. External comparisons and long fuzz remain at existing composed/scheduled gates.

method.kind: Read-only web research plus append-only plan update
method.limitations: Documentation and mutable project pages establish declared route boundaries, not runtime behavior. No result establishes a new libdxfrw defect, native acceptance, or DWG/DXF/3D support promotion.
